answers.explanation: Weak or noisy signals can make a receiver read a 1 as a 0, or the other way round.
Error detection and correction bits: redundancy the sender computes from the data.
Error detection isn't 100% reliable. A rare pattern of errors can still pass the check.
More redundant bits can catch, and fix, more kinds of error. The cost is extra bits on every frame.
1011001 has four 1s, already even, so the parity bit is 0.
Three 1s is odd, so the parity bit is 1 to make it four.
XOR of all the bits is 1 exactly when there's an odd number of 1s.
Parity only catches an odd number of flipped bits.
That makes it an error correction scheme, not just detection.
Ethernet just drops bad frames. It doesn't retransmit at layer 2.
